media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static metaphor poster.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer — Batch B
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/44.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the actual rendered poster.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: a cracked four-block tower on a near-black blue field makes fragility legible before the text is read. 3–10s: the reader scans upward from the broken MRP base through Better Forecast and Fancier Algorithm to the small AI cap. 10–30s: the large closing sentence reframes the object as a warning about layering improvements onto obsolete logic.
creative.lived_work_moment: A planning team keeps adding forecasting or AI layers while the foundational planning logic remains a source of recurring friction.
creative.reader_payoff: A memorable way to open a discussion about whether the constraint is foundational system logic rather than planner capability.
creative.argument_sequence: Cracked foundation → stacked improvement layers → visible failure propagating upward → blunt reframe that the tools, not planners, may be failing.
creative.utility: Recognition / conversation starter; the compact visual can be revisited when framing a transformation problem.
creative.emotional_trigger: Relief from blame paired with discomfort about technical debt.
creative.transferable_atoms: Use a single physical object whose failure propagates through every layer. Make the operational thesis readable in the object before explaining it. Reserve the smallest layer for the fashionable solution so the hierarchy itself carries the critique.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not reproduce the cracked-block tower, block labels, serif headline, Demand Driven Institute branding, or the exact planner/tool wording.

visual.composition: Centred vertical monument: four offset 3D blocks stack from a large cracked grey base to a small turquoise cap; a large two-line conclusion anchors the lower third.
visual.hierarchy: The monument is dominant, then the oversized conclusion, then block labels; the tricolour footer is only a brand accent.
visual.eye_path: Turquoise AI cap → grey Fancier Algorithm block → ochre Better Forecast block → cracked MRP base → oversized conclusion → footer.
visual.imagery: The isometric blocks are causal metaphor, not decoration: increasing cracks and falling chips imply a structural failure below new technology.
visual.typography: Bold white serif display type supplies gravity; short all-caps layer labels create a technical stack; the conclusion uses very large white serif letters with a dark shadow.
visual.layout: Tall single-column poster with generous negative blue space around the object, no panels or dense reference material.
visual.pacing: One immediate visual claim, then four sequential labels, then a final verbal verdict; it is intentionally low-density.
visual.technical_treatment: Dark navy gradient, halftone/comic texture, black outlines, 3D extrusion, hard cracks and controlled turquoise/ochre contrast.
visual.visual_mechanism: A spatial stack makes a dependency relationship literal: an unstable base cannot reliably support upgrades.
visual.craft_notes: The cracks cross block boundaries so failure feels systemic. The decreasing block size makes the fashionable top layer visually insufficient. The base occupies the largest visual mass, matching the argument.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static five-part AI explainer.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer — Batch B
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/51.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the actual rendered poster.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: the oversized ‘5 SURPRISING TRUTHS’ headline and robot/director scene identify the topic and promise a finite list. 3–10s: blue number discs divide the page into five obvious claims. 10–30s: readers inspect the small decision diagrams and short explanations to find the one closest to their AI adoption concern.
creative.lived_work_moment: A supply-chain leader is reconciling expectations of agentic AI with repetitive decisions, data quality, deployment effort and changing roles.
creative.reader_payoff: Five compact prompts for a more realistic AI implementation conversation, framed as patterns rather than laws in the footer.
creative.argument_sequence: Expectation gap → five observations → small illustrative examples → explicit uncertainty boundary → invitation to identify one’s own reality.
creative.utility: Saveable orientation sheet for an early AI-planning or leadership discussion.
creative.emotional_trigger: Curiosity about surprising truths and reassurance that implementation friction is recognisable rather than unique.
creative.transferable_atoms: Use a numbered series when the reader needs to orient across several distinct considerations. Give each claim a different small visual proof, not a repeated icon. State a visible scope boundary when the observations are non-universal.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the robot/director illustration, headline wording, blue number discs, source-specific claims, or the exact five claim formulations.

visual.composition: Tall white poster: headline and robot/director dashboard vignette at top, five full-width rounded horizontal sections, then a blue question footer.
visual.hierarchy: Headline is largest; numbered discs create section entry points; bolded claim clauses are next; diagrams and body copy are subordinate.
visual.eye_path: Headline → robot/director scene → 1 through 5 in vertical order → question-mark footer.
visual.imagery: Robot, person, dashboard, clipboard, hourglass, tangled data and target icons turn abstract AI conditions into skimmable micro-scenes.
visual.typography: Condensed navy all-caps headline; bold black body with key phrases in cobalt; numbers in large blue circles.
visual.layout: Five rounded pale-blue bands with a left-to-right relationship between a numbered visual, written claim and secondary proof visual.
visual.pacing: A repeated vertical rhythm permits one claim per glance; the footer acts as a deliberate pause rather than a sixth claim.
visual.technical_treatment: Clean flat-vector illustration, navy outlines, white ground, cool-blue panels and small yellow/red/green semantic accents.
visual.visual_mechanism: A finite, numbered checklist turns an ambiguous technology topic into five inspectable implementation conditions.
visual.craft_notes: The lead illustration humanises the topic without carrying the argument alone. Each band uses different diagram geometry, preventing the long list from reading as identical cards. The final ‘patterns, not laws’ qualifier is visible inside the visual.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static formula-maturity progression.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer — Batch B
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/59.png against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the actual rendered progression.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: the very large ‘Outgrowing the Safety Stock Formula’ headline and left-to-right Worse/Best rail expose a provocative progression. 3–10s: five cards reveal a visible succession of formulas and methods. 10–30s: a technically curious reader compares the equations, caveat labels and endpoint policy language.
creative.lived_work_moment: A planner needs to explain why a familiar safety-stock formula may be too coarse for a more forecast-aware decision.
creative.reader_payoff: A visual map of an upgrade path from a simplistic formula to policy choices informed by forecast uncertainty.
creative.argument_sequence: Outdated premise → Level 0 limitation → successive formula refinements → simulation/probabilistic endpoint presented as the preferred destination.
creative.utility: Reference visual for a technical discussion or for remembering where a modelling approach sits on a capability continuum.
creative.emotional_trigger: Professional curiosity and a mild challenge to a formula that feels settled.
creative.transferable_atoms: Place a technical progression on a clearly directional rail. Make each state independently legible with one formula or method, one descriptor and a bounded status. Use a visible endpoint only when the relationship is genuinely ordered.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the exact formulas, the declared ‘best’ endpoint, the bell-curve/bar-chart ornaments, or the same worse-to-best colour progression without independent technical verification.

visual.composition: Wide horizontal white canvas: large title above a single five-node maturity rail, with a faded bell curve at left and rising bar chart at right.
visual.hierarchy: Headline dominates, then the coloured directional rail and five large level cards; equations are the close-read layer.
visual.eye_path: Title → Worse label and Level 0 card → cards 1–3 along the blue rail → green Level 4 endpoint → Best label and upward chart.
visual.imagery: The faint statistical bell curve and rising bars function as contextual cues; the cards and formulas do the explanatory work.
visual.typography: Heavy rounded sans headline, subdued blue subtitle, large serif mathematical notation, and simple card labels with blue/green/red emphasis.
visual.layout: A single ordered axis organizes five evenly spaced rounded cards; generous white margin stops technical notation becoming visually oppressive.
visual.pacing: Fast direction at thumbnail size, then optional formula inspection from left to right; the design has no unrelated side panels.
visual.technical_treatment: Soft blue-white gradient, hairline rounded card borders, high-key translucency, blue rail, red failure marker and green endpoint marker.
visual.visual_mechanism: A maturity rail makes a technical replacement argument legible as successive capability states rather than an unstructured equation dump.
visual.craft_notes: The horizontal rail supplies a strong reading contract. Icon-only circular markers above each card keep the line connected without repeating full labels. Red and green are used only for the two endpoints.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static prompt-and-comparison reference sheet.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer — Batch B
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/47.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the actual rendered poster.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: ‘You’re working harder than you need to’ creates a personal cost claim, while the red/green comparison bar signals a before/after proof. 3–10s: the reader matches familiar industrial-engineering tasks to the Without/With Claude table. 10–30s: the lower prompt rows offer copyable starting material task by task.
creative.lived_work_moment: An industrial engineer spends hours creating or analysing recurring artifacts such as a VSM, FMEA, root-cause analysis, SOP or OEE calculation.
creative.reader_payoff: A dense, task-specific reference that combines a contrast in workflow with prompt starters for several named methods.
creative.argument_sequence: Personal workload tension → explicit old/new comparison → promise of reusable prompts → eight task rows → methodology credentialing and save/share prompt.
creative.utility: A practical reference to revisit beside a work task, rather than a general AI inspiration post.
creative.emotional_trigger: Recognition of tedious work paired with hope of retaining methodological quality while reducing setup time.
creative.transferable_atoms: Start a how-to with a contrast between an existing task and a changed workflow. Name the real work artifacts. Place directly usable examples below the proof, so the reader can save one visual for both orientation and execution.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the exact task list, time claims, supplied prompts, red/green comparison table, signature orange starburst, or author branding.

visual.composition: Cream editorial page: brand line and centred italic tension at top; a wide red-header comparison table; a dense lower half of eight labelled prompt rows; author/footer strip.
visual.hierarchy: The italic tension and red comparison band take the first scan; task labels and monospaced prompt lines make up the close-read layer.
visual.eye_path: Series title → tension statement → Without/With comparison → ‘copy these exact prompts’ divider → individual method labels and prompts → methodology footer.
visual.imagery: Nearly all value is typographic; sparse symbols and a coral starburst provide accent without competing with the instructional table.
visual.typography: Mixed editorial serif/italic headline, compact sans explanatory copy, red all-caps label system and monospaced-looking prompt text create a document feel.
visual.layout: Strong horizontal rules turn the poster into a structured worksheet; two columns become a single full-width list after the comparison.
visual.pacing: The top resolves the reason to care; the lower rows deliberately slow the reader into a reference-reading mode.
visual.technical_treatment: Warm off-white paper, brick-red dividers and labels, black type, faint grid/rules, modest icon use and highly restrained accent colour.
visual.visual_mechanism: A true task-by-task before/after creates credibility, while the prompt inventory converts the concept into a saveable working sheet.
visual.craft_notes: The visual uses typographic contrast as an organisational tool rather than decoration. The bold task labels form a left-side index. The lower list has enough density to earn saving but maintains a predictable row grammar.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static procurement decision tree.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer — Batch B
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/54.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the actual rendered decision tree.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: the huge ‘Claude’ title on black and the central question make the post look like a usable chooser rather than an essay. 3–10s: the viewer follows white tree lines through a first task-depth branch and a second complexity branch. 10–30s: leaf cards add concrete task examples, input modes and prompt examples.
creative.lived_work_moment: A procurement practitioner is unsure which AI model or working mode fits a quick communication task, deeper analysis or a file-based workflow.
creative.reader_payoff: An at-a-glance branching route from task characteristics to an intended tool/mode, with examples near each decision.
creative.argument_sequence: Title and purpose → two gating questions → Yes/No branches → model/mode leaf cards → prompt and token-saving tips → branded CTA.
creative.utility: Task-routing reference; the reader can return with a work item and follow a short decision path.
creative.emotional_trigger: Relief from tool-choice ambiguity and confidence from seeing a familiar decision process.
creative.transferable_atoms: Use a decision tree only when two or three observable conditions can route the reader to genuinely different next actions. Pair each leaf with concrete examples. Make branch labels visually unmissable and keep the decision questions above the options.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the exact Claude model names, version numbers, branch wording, orange/green dark theme, prompt examples, or Supply Chain AI Pro branding.

visual.composition: Tall black poster with a centred two-question branching tree; light question cards sit above multiple orange/green action cards and a warm branded footer.
visual.hierarchy: Large ‘Claude for Procurement AI’ title comes first, then the two cream questions and thick white paths, then model cards, then the small prompt cards.
visual.eye_path: Title → first cream decision question → left Sonnet branch or right second question → Haiku/Opus cards → lower task/mode cards → tips and footer.
visual.imagery: Small line icons inside leaf cards signal emails, files, chat, web search, people, upload and prompts; the tree geometry is the primary visual proof.
visual.typography: Large editorial serif title contrasts with compact sans decision labels; dark cards use high-contrast cream/white text and strong all-caps Yes/No tags.
visual.layout: A hierarchical tree with white connectors; lower cards form a staggered reference grid rather than a uniform list.
visual.pacing: The first two questions are scan-fast; detail increases progressively toward the leaves, allowing readers to stop once their route is clear.
visual.technical_treatment: Charcoal ground, cream question cards, coral/orange model cards, dark green task cards, thin white outlines and an orange footer bar.
visual.visual_mechanism: The visible branching logic prevents a complex tool-selection question from becoming a flat list of options.
visual.craft_notes: Branch labels are isolated in bright red/green chips at the moments of choice. Multiple leaf sizes match the different amount of supporting detail. The asymmetric right branch conveys deeper analysis without adding a third decision level.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static strategic-procurement transformation board.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer — Batch B
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/56.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the actual seven-section poster.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: the oversized tactical-to-strategic title and chess/target imagery set up an identity transformation. 3–10s: seven numbered dark-blue section headers turn the surface into a diagnostic map. 10–30s: the reader scans red crosses versus green checks, stop/go pairs and quotation swaps for specific language or metrics to change.
creative.lived_work_moment: A procurement team feels it is viewed as an order-processing function and needs to diagnose the evidence, language and measures that reinforce that perception.
creative.reader_payoff: A broad self-assessment with symptoms, desired business experience, behaviour shifts, language shifts, metrics and a final checklist.
creative.argument_sequence: Perception problem → tactical symptoms → strategic future state → five behavioural shifts → language substitution → metric substitution → checklist.
creative.utility: Workshop or self-diagnosis resource that can be shared across a procurement team.
creative.emotional_trigger: Recognition of a status problem and motivation to demonstrate a more strategic contribution.
creative.transferable_atoms: For a complex maturity/identity change, turn each claim into a visible contrast: cross/check, stop/go, old/new language or old/new metric. Use section numbers as a retrieval map, not just decoration.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the chess/target motif, exact seven-section sequence, language examples, green/red coding scheme, footer CTA or author attribution.

visual.composition: Dense blue-and-white poster: a full-width headline, then a 3-column top diagnostic row, a mid-page stop/go and speech-bubble comparison, and lower metric/checklist panels.
visual.hierarchy: The yellow tactical-to-strategic phrase is the first contrast; oversized 1–7 section numerals and navy bands then segment the dense content.
visual.eye_path: Headline → first three diagnostic panels → sections 4 and 5 across the middle → sections 6 and 7 along the bottom → footer.
visual.imagery: Chess pieces and target at the top metaphorically signal strategic positioning; crosses, ticks, stop signs, arrows and speech bubbles make later contrasts quickly legible.
visual.typography: Condensed white all-caps headers on navy bands, mixed-weight sans body copy, and yellow highlighter treatment for key diagnostic sentences.
visual.layout: Bordered newspaper-like grid with unequal modules: broad three-column diagnosis above tightly packed two-column transformation and checklist sections.
visual.pacing: Requires an initial skim of large numbered bands; then supports non-linear lookup by section rather than a strict narrative read.
visual.technical_treatment: Bright cyan/royal-blue ground, black framing rules, white panels, green/red semantic marks, yellow highlight bands and dense black text.
visual.visual_mechanism: A multiple-contrast transformation board lets the reader find evidence of both the current perception and the desired operating posture.
visual.craft_notes: The grid creates density without losing navigation because every cell begins with a dark label band. Green and red mean change direction consistently. The highlighter strips rescue pivotal sentences from a lot of small text.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static grid of LinkedIn do/don't pairs.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer — Batch B
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/57.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the actual 18-cell sheet.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: ‘18 LinkedIn Laws’ sits oversized in a large central black tile and communicates a finite reference collection. 3–10s: surrounding headings form a twelve-topic menu. 10–30s: each small dark card offers one green DO and one red DON’T for a selected topic.
creative.lived_work_moment: A creator wants a compact checklist of choices across formats, hooks, cadence, engagement and profile behaviour.
creative.reader_payoff: A one-screen reference that enables fast retrieval of one rule at a time rather than a long linear tutorial.
creative.argument_sequence: Central promise → topical tile selection → paired do/don’t instructions → subtle follow/topic attribution.
creative.utility: Save/revisit tool for checking a specific LinkedIn practice.
creative.emotional_trigger: Comfort from a well-organised rule set and mild urgency from the red anti-patterns.
creative.transferable_atoms: A hub-and-surround grid works when the content consists of independently useful rules. Give each tile a consistent positive/negative pair so a reader can scan, save and return non-linearly.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the ‘18 LinkedIn Laws’ title, black-and-cream editorial card style, exact rules, green/red check-cross treatment, or author/topic footer.

visual.composition: Charcoal poster with a large central title tile surrounded by twelve equally styled rounded rectangles in a near-grid.
visual.hierarchy: The central ‘18 LinkedIn Laws’ tile is much larger; topic headings are secondary; coloured check/cross symbols create quick third-level anchors.
visual.eye_path: Centre title → adjacent headings around the grid → individual green DO line and red DON’T line within a chosen tile → small footer.
visual.imagery: No illustrative scenes; symbols, rounded card boundaries and typographic hierarchy provide all the visual structure.
visual.typography: Large high-contrast serif display type for title/topic headings and compact serif body text; green and red symbols distinguish instruction polarity.
visual.layout: A modular 4-column-like field with the title occupying the central large tile and independent advice tiles around it.
visual.pacing: The layout rejects a single narrative order; it rewards scanning to the relevant problem and returning later for another tile.
visual.technical_treatment: Near-black textured ground, thin cream outlines, cream text, pale green checks, red crosses and very restrained colour.
visual.visual_mechanism: A central index plus surrounding modules makes a dense checklist feel like a reference board rather than an article.
visual.craft_notes: The empty black spaces between rounded cards preserve legibility. Title scale creates immediate recognisability at thumbnail size. Strictly repeated card grammar creates reliability across many content units.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static ten-step procurement roadmap.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer — Batch B
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/52.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the actual numbered roadmap.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: oversized condensed ‘PROCUREMENT WITH CLAUDE’ and a taped ‘IN 7 DAYS’ label create a bold transformation promise. 3–10s: numbered circles 01–10 identify an ordered programme. 10–30s: readers choose a step and inspect its folder, prompt, workflow or habit micro-details.
creative.lived_work_moment: A procurement professional wants an ordered starting plan for setting up an AI-supported way of working rather than isolated prompts.
creative.reader_payoff: A structured ten-move route covering workspace, file system, documents, prompts, workflows and iteration.
creative.argument_sequence: Transformation promise → steps 1–10 in numeric order → task-specific bullets and mini-templates → brand/footer CTA.
creative.utility: A broad onboarding roadmap that can be saved and revisited sequentially.
creative.emotional_trigger: Momentum from an apparently finite programme and reassurance that there is a starting point.
creative.transferable_atoms: Use an ordered roadmap when prerequisites matter. Combine a large sequence number with one task headline and a small concrete output, keeping the same visual slot across steps.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the exact ten-step curriculum, ‘in 7 days’ promise, Claude branding, dark-blue/orange palette, task examples, or footer design.

visual.composition: Tall navy poster with a huge headline band above ten numbered cells arranged in five horizontal rows of two, plus a branded orange footer.
visual.hierarchy: Largest elements are Procurement/Claude and the taped time promise; pale-blue number discs and bold step labels guide the mid-level read; bullets and quote boxes are close-read detail.
visual.eye_path: Headline → first row (01/02) → successive paired rows downward → lower daily-flow step → footer.
visual.imagery: Folders, chat, file, cowork, code, gear, chart and calendar icons identify work objects; boxed mini-templates ground abstract steps.
visual.typography: Very condensed white all-caps title, white sans step headings, pale-blue circular numbers and smaller explanatory copy on dark blue.
visual.layout: A tightly ruled two-column roadmap; each row contains an unequal amount of text but consistent number/title/icon placement.
visual.pacing: The top creates aspiration; 10 numbered compartments permit either sequential study or targeted lookup; details repeat a predictable visual grammar.
visual.technical_treatment: Deep navy ground, white rule grid, pale-blue number circles and icons, orange taped accent and orange brand footer.
visual.visual_mechanism: A numbered operating roadmap converts a large AI-adoption topic into a sequence of visible work artifacts and habits.
visual.craft_notes: The strong grid prevents the ten topics from blurring. Large step numerals give orientation even when the small copy is unreadable at thumbnail scale. Iconography makes each step distinguishable without another colour system.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static LinkedIn growth blueprint.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer — Batch B
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/50.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the actual multi-module blueprint.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: the oversized ‘How to Grow on LinkedIn’ headline, oversized blue word block and ‘1,000+ accounts’ subtitle create a one-sheet blueprint promise. 3–10s: the reader sees two prominent time-bound modules—the 10-minute audit and 60-minute daily loop. 10–30s: lower modules offer content mix, hooks, engagement, metrics, week plan and creator-follow list.
creative.lived_work_moment: A creator is looking for a repeatable weekly LinkedIn operating rhythm across profile, publishing, response and measurement.
creative.reader_payoff: A broad workflow map that gives several possible next actions within one saved visual.
creative.argument_sequence: Big growth promise → immediate profile audit → daily loop → tactical content/engagement modules → metrics and weekly plan → creator list and CTA.
creative.utility: Reference board to return to when planning a week or auditing one part of a content operation.
creative.emotional_trigger: Ambition with relief that a complex growth routine has been made into bounded time blocks.
creative.transferable_atoms: Group a broad operating system into unequal functional modules and make the time-bound routine visually dominant. Provide both a recurring loop and a planning horizon so the reader can choose a next action.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the 1,000+ account claim, exact minute allocation, Stanley branding, named creator list, quote-ready hook examples, or blue/teal blueprint treatment.

visual.composition: Pale blue poster with a large mixed-type headline, two full-width rounded modules at top, then six smaller modules in a three-column lower grid and a cobalt footer.
visual.hierarchy: Headline and blue ‘Grow on LinkedIn’ label lead; the profile audit and daily loop span the width; lower boxes are an intentionally secondary reference shelf.
visual.eye_path: Headline → profile audit → daily loop broken into time columns → three middle modules → three bottom modules → branded footer.
visual.imagery: Small black outline icons clarify profile, clock, hook, handshake, metrics and people without carrying the rationale.
visual.typography: Large black display serif paired with bold blue serif in a rounded word container; module titles use bold sans and dense body copy.
visual.layout: A visual operating manual: wide modules hold a sequence and small modules hold independent reference material.
visual.pacing: Starts with an overview, moves to daily behaviour, then invites non-linear lookup in the lower tile field.
visual.technical_treatment: Pale ice-blue background, cobalt borders/shadows and headings, teal-to-blue panel tints, black icon line work and sparse yellow highlighter accents.
visual.visual_mechanism: The sheet packages a multi-part system as a spatial dashboard so readers can navigate by operating job rather than read a long post in order.
visual.craft_notes: Time chips divide the daily loop into clear action windows. Repeated rounded borders make uneven content feel coherent. The giant blue title block provides thumbnail contrast while the lower field provides saving value.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static three-layer planning framework.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer — Batch B
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/46.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the actual planning-engine infographic.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: the oversized ‘3-Layer Planning Engine’ headline and three vertically stacked coloured blocks establish an organisational model. 3–10s: arrows imply a demand-to-supply-to-execution sequence while a row of industry icons broadens applicability. 10–30s: readers inspect the components, trade-offs, failure panel and bottom operating loop.
creative.lived_work_moment: A supply-chain practitioner needs a plain-language map of how demand, supply and execution planning connect, and where local optimisation can fail the network.
creative.reader_payoff: A single visual reference tying three planning layers to inputs, decisions, failure modes and a continuous response loop.
creative.argument_sequence: Broad applicability → three layers and their questions → components and balancing variables → organisational failure pattern / alternative practices → sense-simulate-decide-adapt outcome loop.
creative.utility: Orientation resource for explaining planning architecture to a colleague or using as a shared vocabulary in an improvement discussion.
creative.emotional_trigger: Clarity from seeing a complicated operating system in a familiar vertical stack and concern about siloed local optimisation.
creative.transferable_atoms: When a system has dependent layers, use a strict spatial stack and repeat one question per layer. Place exceptions or contrast panels to the side so they inform the core flow without breaking it. Use an outcome loop only after the system is clear.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the exact 3-layer headings, specific claims about leading organisations, icon taxonomy, green/blue/purple layer palette, or headline/footer language.

visual.composition: Tall white canvas: huge navy/blue headline, small industry icon strip, three wide stacked modules down the left two-thirds, comparison/exception panels along the right, and a bottom continuous-loop band.
visual.hierarchy: Headline and coloured vertical layer labels lead; large layer labels and arrows form the second scan; component icons, side panels and outcome loop are close-read detail.
visual.eye_path: Title → industry applicability strip → green Demand block → blue Supply block → purple Execution block → lower Sense/Simulate/Decide/Adapt strip and side outcome panel.
visual.imagery: Factory, truck, cart, supplier and other operational icons identify industries and planning tasks; arrows and balance symbols encode relationships.
visual.typography: Extra-bold condensed sans for headline; broad all-caps layer tags; smaller bold sans for components and goals; coloured keywords reinforce hierarchy.
visual.layout: A primary 3-step vertical process is accompanied by two narrow right-side ‘struggle’/‘doing differently’ cards and a footer-sized outcome loop.
visual.pacing: Readers receive the model in three large sweeps first, then can fan out into layers, side diagnosis and bottom operating cycle.
visual.technical_treatment: White ground, navy title bands and arrows, dark green/blue/purple semantic layer fields, small flat-vector icons and pale bordered content panels.
visual.visual_mechanism: A vertical architecture diagram makes dependency and handoff visible, then adds side evidence about what degrades when layers are disconnected.
visual.craft_notes: The left rail carries the main causal flow and has the largest surface area. Side panels are visibly subordinate through their narrower width. Arrows between modules enforce an order even with a lot of internal detail.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static six-principle procurement guide.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer — Batch B
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/49.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the actual six-panel guide.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: large numeral ‘6’ and dark headline promise a finite practical guide. 3–10s: six differently coloured headers make the principles easy to index. 10–30s: each large panel offers one action, a compact diagram and a short explanatory takeaway.
creative.lived_work_moment: A procurement team is deciding where to begin with AI and needs an accessible sequence from problem definition to a sustainable foundation.
creative.reader_payoff: Six operational principles with a visual mnemonic for each, useful as an early adoption checklist.
creative.argument_sequence: Guide promise → process before tools → narrow one use case → map current workflow → choose entry point → repeat/measure → build data/governance foundation.
creative.utility: Saveable checklist for setting up or reviewing a procurement AI initiative.
creative.emotional_trigger: Confidence from a simple progression and reassurance that starting narrow is legitimate.
creative.transferable_atoms: Use a 2×3 field when six principles are comparable but each benefits from a unique explanatory mini-diagram. Give each module a concrete ‘Try this’ instruction and keep the progression visible in numbering rather than an artificial flowchart.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the exact six principles, procurement-specific prompts, coloured header palette, Supply Chain AI Pro footer, model icons or wording.

visual.composition: Cream portrait poster: large title above a balanced 2×3 grid of white rounded panels; each panel has a saturated colour header, number circle, instructional copy and mini-diagram.
visual.hierarchy: Title and the six bright header bars lead; bold ‘Try this’ labels create a second level; small checklists/diagrams and footer are third-level.
visual.eye_path: Title → panels 1 and 2 left/right → panels 3 and 4 → panels 5 and 6 → orange footer.
visual.imagery: Each panel uses an operational schematic: problem node, too-broad funnel, circular workflow map, impact funnel, time chart or foundation icon grid.
visual.typography: Large dark sans title, bold white header text, compact dark body text and consistently large numbered circles.
visual.layout: Six evenly sized instructional tiles create a clear scan pattern, with internal diagrams placed where unused white space permits.
visual.pacing: High-level principle names scan quickly; each tile then supports a short independent close read, without requiring the other five tiles.
visual.technical_treatment: Warm cream background, thin tinted borders, strong purple/green/orange/blue/pink/teal headers, soft pastel info blocks and flat outline icons.
visual.visual_mechanism: A repeated module grammar turns an abstract set of principles into six separately usable small operating aids.
visual.craft_notes: Header colours differentiate without becoming a separate legend. Most panels use a visual model rather than only paragraphs. Consistent round number markers make the order visible despite a grid layout.

creative.utility: A simple roadmap to save while planning a new content programme.
creative.emotional_trigger: Relief from the fear of being overly promotional, combined with a clear time horizon.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static S&OP explainer board.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: giant ‘S&OP PROCESS EXPLAINED’ and a dashboard/calendar cue promise a complete reference rather than a single definition. 3–10s: ten numbered section bands show the sheet covers definition, purpose, participants, steps, inputs, outputs, challenges, KPIs, impact and forecast comparison. 10–30s: the reader picks a module—especially the five-step sequence—to use as a meeting or learning aid.
creative.lived_work_moment: A cross-functional supply-chain participant needs a shared model of S&OP participants, review steps, inputs, outputs and common breakdowns.
creative.reader_payoff: A broad map of S&OP that can orient a new participant or seed a team conversation about the process.
creative.argument_sequence: Definition and value → participating functions → five-step process spine → inputs/outputs/challenges → KPI/impact/forecast illustrations → connected-plan conclusion.
creative.utility: High-density orientation sheet; useful for study, onboarding or setting a meeting agenda.
creative.emotional_trigger: Clarity and professional confidence from seeing a complex cross-functional process decomposed into visible parts.
creative.transferable_atoms: For an operating system with many interconnected parts, preserve one central process spine and let definitions, actors, inputs, outputs and metrics orbit it as labelled modules. Make the process sequence larger than the supporting catalogue.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the S&OP title treatment, exact five-step labels, percentages/metric targets, icon set, dark-blue/turquoise palette, or author/series branding; verify all numerical claims independently.

visual.composition: Tall white sheet with a dark-navy title masthead; early two-column definition/benefits panels; a central five-step horizontal sequence; lower three-column inputs/outputs/challenges and KPI/impact/chart modules.
visual.hierarchy: Title masthead is dominant; the numbered section labels and central five-card process spine are the next strongest elements; support lists and pie/line charts are close-read.
visual.eye_path: Title → what/why top panels → participants and pie → five core steps across the page → inputs/outputs/challenges → KPI/business impact/forecast chart → dark-blue footer.
visual.imagery: Flat operational icons identify functions and steps; the circular demand/supply/financial triad and process arrows show relationships; charts occupy proof-like positions but are not externally verified here.
visual.typography: Condensed white/turquoise all-caps display title; dark navy all-caps module headings; smaller black body copy and bold numerical callouts.
visual.layout: A highly structured magazine grid with wide central process row and three lower columns; large numbered headers make each cluster independently retrievable.
visual.pacing: The top explains the noun, the middle sequences the work, and the lower third becomes a reference catalogue; readers can exit after any level.
visual.technical_treatment: Navy masthead/footer, turquoise-blue section accents, white cards with thin blue rules, saturated icon colours and controlled orange/purple highlights.
visual.visual_mechanism: An explainer board turns an organisational process into a visible map: who participates, what flows in, what happens, what comes out, and what can derail it.
visual.craft_notes: Numbered headers provide a robust index across very different modules. The five-step sequence uses large arrows and equally sized cards to make the operating flow legible at a glance. The dense lower panels retain an aligned column grid.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: the billboard-sized ‘THE FORMAT SWEET SPOT’ headline and saturated blue blueprint surface promise a compressed answer. 3–10s: eight named content formats appear as paired left/right panels while oversized numbers announce the proposed parameter for each. 10–30s: the reader compares one parameter at a time and notices the source note at the base.
creative.lived_work_moment: A LinkedIn creator is selecting content formats and wants a quick constraint or cadence cue rather than a long research report.
creative.reader_payoff: A one-screen comparison of several LinkedIn formats and the source author’s proposed usage parameters.
creative.argument_sequence: One-screen promise → eight format cards with a hero metric → small rule/explanation per format → source/dataset line.
creative.utility: Fast comparison reference, with an obvious need to verify or contextualise quantitative recommendations before acting on them.
creative.emotional_trigger: Decision relief from a tidy set of comparable format choices.
creative.transferable_atoms: When several comparable options each have one primary variable, use a uniform metric-card system and reserve extreme type for the actual choice variable. Keep source information visible and distinguish observed data from recommendations.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the exact numeric recommendations, research/source assertions, blue grid background, oversized-number card treatment, or author logo. Do not treat the visual alone as validation of its performance claims.

visual.composition: Bright blue grid poster with a full-width white title, then eight translucent rectangular format cards in four rows, bridged by large blue circular icons through the centre.
visual.hierarchy: White all-caps headline dominates; each card’s giant white number or duration is second; small recommendations and source note are third.
visual.eye_path: Headline → left/right top pair → next paired cards down each side → central circular icon chain → bottom source line.
visual.imagery: Simple white line icons in oversized raised blue circles—document, image, typography, video, poll, article, reshare and microphone—identify formats.

visual.pacing: Fast at title and number level; each panel supports a brief independent look; no strict narrative sequence is required.
visual.technical_treatment: Electric-blue gradient/grid ground, translucent blue cards with white borders, circular drop-shadowed icon buttons and white type throughout.
visual.visual_mechanism: A consistent metric-card system turns format choice into a scanable comparison board rather than prose advice.
visual.craft_notes: The central icon chain creates visual movement between pairs of panels. Oversized figures are disciplined to one per card. The source line is present but too small to qualify as full evidence on its own.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: the large 10,000 Followers headline and peach-highlighted phrase make an aspirational endpoint unmistakable. 3–10s: four wide horizontal stages create a visible progression from 0 to 500 through 5K–10K. 10–30s: each stage exposes content and engagement actions, a short moral, and a final stage-specific measurement table.
creative.lived_work_moment: A new LinkedIn creator wants to know which behaviours and metrics should change as an audience grows.
creative.reader_payoff: A stage-based operating model that differentiates early consistency from later conversion and revenue questions.

creative.utility: Stage-specific checklist to revisit after a follower milestone.
creative.emotional_trigger: Ambition tempered by reassurance that the next step is narrower than the final goal.

creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the 10,000/250+ claims, exact stage thresholds, individual advice, purple/peach pastel treatment, author branding or CTA; do not present the roadmap as a guaranteed growth formula.

visual.visual_mechanism: A self-identification ladder lets the reader locate their current state before consuming recommendations intended for that state.
visual.craft_notes: Each band has a consistent header/action/moral pattern, which makes many small instructions manageable. Distinct pastel fills keep stages separable without a hard chronology line. The lower table translates advice into a measurement contract.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static three-part post system.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer — Batch B
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/42.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the actual three-column workflow guide.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: the extremely large ‘3-Part System’ title and three pastel panels signal a complete before/during/after workflow. 3–10s: readers decode the panel names—Ideation, Going Live, After Posting—and their time-based relationship. 10–30s: they inspect numbered best practices, a pre-post checklist and the final 30-minute response schedule.
creative.lived_work_moment: A LinkedIn creator wants a usable operating routine that includes ideation, publishing preparation and the immediate post-publish period.
creative.reader_payoff: One structured workflow showing that a post has preparatory, launch and follow-through work—not merely a writing task.
creative.argument_sequence: System title → prepare an angle from reference material → go-live checks/timing → first 30-minute post-publish actions → future repurposing and target-audience handoff.
creative.utility: Practical post-day checklist that can be scanned in time order.
creative.emotional_trigger: Agency from seeing the hidden work around a post made explicit.
creative.transferable_atoms: Use three columns when a workflow has distinct temporal phases. Give each phase a different background field, a defined job, numbered actions and a small visual process or checklist at the point where uncertainty is highest.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the exact timing claims, platform/tool names, three panel wording, pastel colours, icon illustrations or author/course CTA.

visual.composition: Pale blue portrait sheet with a massive two-line serif title above three full-height pastel columns: lavender Ideation, yellow-green Going Live and mint After Posting.
visual.hierarchy: Title is dominant; large phase names plus a single icon per column are second; section bars and numbered action cards are the close-read layers.
visual.eye_path: Title → left Ideation column → centre Going Live column → right After Posting column → bottom CTA strip.
visual.imagery: Illustrated lightbulb, calendar/clock and stopwatch establish phases; lower left includes a circular process doodle and lower centre/right include checklists/time bar.
visual.typography: High-contrast dark serif display type for title/phase labels; rounded sans for section bars, explanatory copy and blue numbered discs.
visual.layout: Three equal columns use identical header/body/footer structure but custom lower modules appropriate to each phase.
visual.pacing: The design reads left to right as a timeline, but every column supports independent scanning; numbered cards slow the reader where operational detail matters.
visual.technical_treatment: Powder-blue outer ground, lavender/chartreuse/mint internal fields, navy type, pale rounded text boxes, dotted divider lines and hand-drawn illustration accents.
visual.visual_mechanism: Temporal columns make the invisible lifecycle of a post visible, turning generic ‘just post’ advice into a repeatable work sequence.
visual.craft_notes: The columns are large enough to preserve phase identity. The centre panel contains a visible pre-post checklist and the right panel uses a 10/10/10 response bar, so the reader sees not only what but when.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: the huge ‘How to build your Procurement AI copilot with Claude’ headline and orange Claude word object signal a ready-to-build artifact. 3–10s: a left-side 2×5 capability grid and right-side dark code window establish a two-part promise: components and setup. 10–30s: the reader matches pairs of operational capabilities to configuration rules, then finds a fill-in prompt and three example applications.
creative.lived_work_moment: A procurement practitioner wants to articulate the components, constraints and output format of an AI assistant rather than rely on isolated chat requests.
creative.reader_payoff: A visible scaffold for thinking about capabilities, guardrails and a configuration prompt—without claiming that the depicted assistant is already deployed.
creative.argument_sequence: Build promise → paired capability list → pseudo-configuration file with numbered sections → copyable setup prompt → three practical application cards.
creative.utility: A design reference for drafting requirements or a working instruction file for a procurement assistant.
creative.emotional_trigger: Control and confidence from seeing a vague ‘copilot’ converted into named functions and constraints.
creative.transferable_atoms: For a system-design post, juxtapose user-facing capabilities with the governing configuration that creates them. Use a code-like or document-like artifact only when it represents a real editable object, and make guardrails as visible as benefits.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the Claude name/logo treatment, exact capability list, pseudo-file wording, orange/black component styling, author footer or any unverified automation claims.

visual.eye_path: Title → left capability pairs and right configuration panel in parallel → orange ‘paste this’ banner → lower three application cards → footer.

visual.layout: Asymmetric two-column comparison: narrower functional cards versus a larger code/configuration object, united by repeated orange numbered markers.
visual.pacing: The headline invites the read, the left/right comparison gives the architecture, and the lower banner offers an immediate first action.
visual.technical_treatment: Warm cream ground, orange outlines/number discs, black code window with traffic-light dots, rounded white cards, orange CTA band and dark application tiles.
visual.visual_mechanism: A capability-to-configuration pairing makes an assistant feel concrete by showing both what it does and the rules that should shape it.
visual.craft_notes: Repeated numbers visually link left pairs to right-side code sections. The visual uses strong orange only for build signals and action areas. Distinct document/code/app surfaces make the post feel like a working blueprint, not a decorative list.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: the large ‘WHY some posts convert better’ title turns a vague content question into a business-outcome promise. 3–10s: a visibly connected tool-flow shows content tools converging into LinkedIn and a lead-tracking system. 10–30s: the lower product dashboard provides a concrete imagined/claimed view of the resulting attribution and feedback loop.
creative.lived_work_moment: A B2B creator or marketer wants to know which content is influencing pipeline rather than stopping at impressions and reactions.
creative.reader_payoff: A clear conceptual map of how publishing inputs could connect to content-attribution outputs and inform future topic choices.

creative.emotional_trigger: Relief from measurement ambiguity and desire for a closer connection between content and revenue.

creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy tool logos, product screenshots, fictional customer/lead rows, dashboard figures, the exact flow arrows or any attribution claim without independent proof.

visual.composition: Tall white dotted-grid canvas: title and premise at top; a top-half system flow with five content-tool logos converging to LinkedIn and Sociale​ads.io; a large dashboard/product view fills the lower half; a final feedback instruction sits at the bottom.

visual.eye_path: Title → content-tool row → LinkedIn plus tracking logos → highlighted output statement → dashboard panels/right post card → bottom feedback loop.

visual.pacing: Readers first understand the system topology, then dwell on the evidence-like dashboard detail, then see the return loop that makes it an operating system.

visual.visual_mechanism: A visible closed loop makes the abstract assertion ‘engagement is not business impact’ easier to grasp as a measurable systems problem.
visual.craft_notes: The lower mockup is intentionally large enough to act as a proof object, even though its numbers must not be treated as verified evidence. Curved return arrows turn a one-way pipeline into a learning loop. The dotted grid supports a technical blueprint feel.

media.availability_note: Directly inspected local Top-100 asset: a single static procurement AI MVP guide.

review.reviewer: Codex direct-asset visual reviewer — Batch B
review.evidence: Full-size direct inspection of references/top 100/34.jpeg against the declared SHA-256; observations below describe the actual six-stage MVP guide.

creative.attention_mechanism: 0–3s: ‘How To Build A Procurement AI MVP’ plus the Pain Point → MVP → Value line makes a business-oriented transformation visible. 3–10s: six colour-coded numbered panels show a full narrow-to-scale sequence. 10–30s: each panel supplies a checklist, good/bad contrast or small loop; the reader can locate the stage currently blocking a pilot.
creative.lived_work_moment: A procurement leader is trying to turn broad AI interest into a narrowly scoped, validated pilot that can gain support and scale responsibly.
creative.reader_payoff: A staged checklist for choosing a high-value problem, validating it, defining an MVP, planning a pilot, learning and scaling with governance.
creative.argument_sequence: High-value problem → validate pain/opportunity → define one core MVP → build CPO business case/pilot → measure/learn/iterate → scale with governance → narrow/fast/responsible summary.

creative.emotional_trigger: Confidence that a small pilot can be legitimate, tempered by guardrails around scope and governance.
creative.transferable_atoms: For an innovation process, use a visible value chain at the top and a set of step panels that each contain one concrete decision, a test/criterion and an anti-pattern. End with a shorter three-part mnemonic that restates the overall discipline.
creative.anti_copy_boundary: Do not copy the exact six-step MVP sequence, buyer-interview counts, implementation durations, good/bad example, multi-colour panel palette, footer copy or author branding; validate all numeric or causal claims separately.

visual.hierarchy: Title and top value chain lead; numbered coloured panel headings are second; checklists, diagrams and prompt-like callouts form the close-read layer.

visual.pacing: Top-down overview first; panels permit stage-specific lookup; bottom summary closes the loop with a memorable three-part rule.
visual.technical_treatment: Cream paper ground, thin coloured rounded borders, blue/green/gold/orange/pink/purple headings, pale highlighted checklists and a small orange brand footer.
visual.visual_mechanism: A staged pilot map gives shape to a fuzzy AI project by separating problem validation, product scope, economic approval, learning and governance.
visual.craft_notes: The three-node chain establishes a visual thesis before detail. Each panel has a unique evidence device, preventing repetition: checklists, comparison, loop, and priority list. Coloured borders make a dense six-part board independently navigable.
